summary: Refreshing the Project Instance dataset table is far faster on network-drive installs, and the table no longer goes stale until you refresh it.
details: Reloading the dataset table now lists the reserving-class folders and rebuilds index.json only when something actually changed on disk, instead of re-reading every sidecar and method file every time.

An unchanged reserving class reloads with three directory listings instead of roughly 450 filesystem operations, which is where the multi-second wait after the refresh button and after Import ResQ Reserving Class came from.

A rebuild that is still needed costs about a third of what it used to: the folder listing's file sizes and timestamps are reused instead of re-read one file at a time, and the project and reserving-class folders are no longer enumerated twice per request.
Dataset files written by the ArcRho Bridge, migration, or another user now appear on the next dataset table read rather than only after a manual refresh.
